definition_zh: 陈腐的；平庸乏味的；老生常谈的
definition_en: lacking originality because repeated too often; dull and commonplace
core_image: 一句被说了一万遍的话，说出时已经没有声音
scene: 贺卡摊前翻来翻去，每张都是同一句祝福。She found the message sweet but banal.
sceneCN: 这里 banal 指「陈腐乏味的」（第 1 个义项：因重复而失去新意）；句意：她觉得这条祝福温暖却俗套。

senses.title: Worn out by repetition
senses.definition: dull because said or done so many times that nothing is left
senses.definitionCN: 因说了太多遍而失味的；老套的
senses.example: The speech was full of banal slogans.
senses.exampleCN: 演讲里满是陈腐的口号。
senses.why: The word's first life named common obligations owed by all, and commonness stayed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的初义指人人共担的义务，「共通」之意留了下来。

senses.title: Of ordinary, everyday things
senses.definition: belonging to the ordinary, everyday level of life
senses.example: The film finds beauty in banal scenes of cooking and cleaning.
senses.exampleCN: 影片在做饭打扫这些平常场景里发现美。
senses.why: Old French banal meant of the communal oven and mill: the shared, the ordinary.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 banal 本指公共炉灶与磨坊：共用的、寻常的。

senses.title: Of talk that says nothing
senses.definition: of remarks or writing, empty of thought though dressed in words
senses.definitionCN: 指言辞徒有其表、没有思想内容
senses.example: His letters were polite but banal.
senses.exampleCN: 他的信礼貌周到却言之无物。
senses.why: When the communal word is used again, it carries no one's thought.
senses.whyCN: 公共的词再用一遍，已载不动任何人的思想。

senses.title: Of art without fresh vision
senses.definition: of artworks, conventional in image or treatment
senses.definitionCN: 指作品意象或手法落入俗套
senses.example: Critics called the sunset scenes banal.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家批评那些日落场景俗不可耐。
senses.why: Criticism adopted the word in the nineteenth century to judge newness.
senses.whyCN: 19 世纪批评界采用此词来衡量「新意」。

senses.title: The banality of evil
senses.definition: in the phrase the banality of evil, wrongdoing done by unthinking ordinary people
senses.definitionCN: 「平庸之恶」：由不加思考的普通人犯下的恶行
senses.example: Hannah Arendt named the banality of evil in her report on the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 汉娜·阿伦特在庭审报道中提出「平庸之恶」。
senses.why: Arendt saw that great crimes can be committed by clerks repeating phrases.
senses.whyCN: 阿伦特看到滔天罪行可由照章办事的职员之手完成。

senses.title: Once common to all, the legal sense
senses.definition: in medieval usage, of facilities open to all tenants, as a communal oven
senses.definitionCN: 中世纪用法：指供全体佃户使用的公用设施
senses.example: The banal mill ground every family's grain for a fee.
senses.exampleCN: 公用磨坊收费为每户碾谷。
senses.why: This is the word's first sense, before criticism bent it toward contempt.
senses.whyCN: 这是词的初义，后被批评界扭向轻蔑。

senses.title: Banality as a noun of things
senses.definition: in banality, a remark or thing that is banal
senses.definitionCN: 名词 banality：一句陈词滥调或一件平庸之物
senses.example: Every banality he uttered was received as wisdom.
senses.exampleCN: 他说出的每一句套话都被当作智慧接收。
senses.why: The adjective made so many nouns that it earned its own.
senses.whyCN: 形容词造出太多平庸之物，于是自己也有了专名。

senses.title: Banally, the flat adverb
senses.definition: in banally, in a trite or predictable manner
senses.definitionCN: 副词 banally：以陈腐可测的方式
senses.example: The dialogue ends banally, with everyone forgiven.
senses.exampleCN: 对白以人人得到原谅的老套方式收场。
senses.why: Adverbs record manner, and triteness is a manner.
senses.whyCN: 副词记录方式，而陈腐正是一种方式。

intro.en: Banal comes from Old French ban, a lord's public summons, later the fee for using his facilities; banal first meant belonging to such common facilities, and only in the nineteenth century did critics turn the shared into the worn-out.
intro.cn: banal 出自古法语 ban「领主的公共召集令」，后指使用其设施的规费；banal 最初意为「属公共设施之用的」，至 19 世纪批评界才把「共用」扭成「用滥」。

items.en: The Germanic verb bannan meant to command under penalty; it gives English ban.
items.cn: 日耳曼动词 bannan 意为以罚相令；英语 ban 即出于此。

items.en: ban named the lord's summons, his jurisdiction, and the levies attached to it.
items.cn: 古法语 ban 指领主的召集令、辖权及随附的规费。

items.en: banal described facilities all tenants had to use and pay for, as the communal oven.
items.cn: banal 形容全体佃户必须使用并付费的公共设施，如公共烤炉。

items.en: French extended banal from communal to common to commonplace.
items.cn: 法语中 banal 由「公用的」引申为「平常的」再到「平庸的」。

items.en: English borrowed the legal sense first; the critical sense of triteness hardened by the mid-nineteenth century.
items.cn: 英语先借入法权义；「陈腐」的批评义至 19 世纪中叶定型。

items.en: Arendt's banality of evil in 1963 gave the word its most famous modern phrase.
items.cn: 1963 年阿伦特的「平庸之恶」赋予该词最著名的现代用法。

note.en: Group one holds the ban-root family and look-alikes; group two holds the triteness field.
note.cn: 第一组收 ban 词根词族与形近词；第二组收「陈腐」义场的词。

entries.definition: to forbid; the Germanic verb beneath the French line.
entries.definitionCN: 禁止；法语词线下面的日耳曼动词。

entries.definition: a printed cloth; from Hindi, only the spelling misleads.
entries.definitionCN: 印花方巾；出自印地语，仅拼写相近，词源无关。

entries.definition: marriage announcements; the old summons survives here.
entries.definitionCN: 结婚预告；古老的召集令在此幸存。

entries.definition: the fruit; from a West African language, no kin to ban.
entries.definitionCN: 香蕉；出自西非语言，与 ban 词根无关。

entries.definition: worn out from use; the closest cousin.
entries.definitionCN: 用旧了的；最近义的表亲。

entries.definition: made dull by too much hiring-out of phrases.
entries.definitionCN: 因被反复出租而变乏味的。

entries.definition: cast too often, like a printing plate.
a stale accepted truth; the noun field.
entries.definitionCN: 陈腐的套话；名词义场的同类。

entries.definition: fresh and new; the direct antonym.

normalIntro.en: banal is ban plus the French adjective tail: the summoned crowd, all saying the same thing.
normalIntro.cn: banal 即 ban 加法语形容词尾：被召集的人群，说的都是同一句话。

normal.en: Root: Germanic bannan, to command, through French ban.
normal.cn: 词根：日耳曼 bannan「以罚相令」，经法语 ban。

normal.en: First sense: facilities all tenants shared, as the banal oven.
normal.cn: 初义：佃户共用的设施，如公共烤炉。

normal.en: The noun is banality: a stale remark.
normal.cn: 名词 banality 指陈词滥调。

normal.en: Arendt's phrase: the banality of evil.
normal.cn: 阿伦特的名句：the banality of evil（平庸之恶）。

normal.en: Verb banalize: to wear a thought out in public.
normal.cn: 动词 banalize：把一个想法 publicly 用旧。

abstract.en: Hear a sentence repeated until it stops meaning.
abstract.cn: 听一句话被重复到不再有意义的时刻。

abstract.en: Banal is the crowd's echo wearing one voice.
abstract.cn: banal 是穿着一副嗓音的人群回声。

abstract.en: See the communal oven: shared by all, owned by none, remarked on by no one.
abstract.cn: 看那座公共烤炉：人人共用，无人拥有，无人评说。

examples.en: The review dismissed the novel's plot as banal.
examples.cn: 书评斥该小说情节陈腐。

examples.en: Even banal details, dates and bus stops, gave the report its power.
examples.cn: 即便是日期与公交站这类平淡细节，也赋予报道以力量。

examples.en: He hid his fear behind banal questions about the weather.
examples.cn: 他用「天气如何」的套话掩饰恐惧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摆弄」——被摆弄了千万遍的话，说出来早没了新意

root: 出自日耳曼词根 bannan「以罚相令」（英语 ban 同源），经古法语 ban「领主召集令、辖权与规费」生出 banal「（公共设施）供全体佃户共用的」；后由「共用」引申为「平常、平庸」，19 世纪经批评界定型为「陈腐的」；与现代义最近的是法语而非拉丁语路线。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the shared to the stale: the communal oven, the ordinary day, the empty phrase, the conventional artwork, the banality of evil, the noun, and the adverb.
sensesIntro.cn: 八义项由「共用」滑向「用滥」：公共烤炉、寻常日子、空话、俗套作品、平庸之恶，以及名词与副词形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thing owned by everyone, used by everyone, noticed by no one.
core.cn: 核心意象：人人共有、人人使用、无人留意之物。

branches.en: THE STALE SIDE: phrases worn to nothing.
branches.cn: 陈腐一面：被磨到无物的语句。

branches.en: THE COMMON SIDE: ovens, mills, and everyday life.
branches.cn: 平常一面：烤炉、磨坊与日常生活。

branches.en: THE CRITICISM SIDE: art and dialogue judged trite.
branches.cn: 批评一面：被判俗套的作品与对白。

branches.en: THE DARK SIDE: evil done on autopilot.
branches.cn: 黑暗一面：自动驾驶般的恶。

branches.en: THE NOUN SIDE: banality as the thing itself.
branches.cn: 名词一面：banality 指平庸之物本身。

intro.en: Banal carries the ban root through French; its English dress is plain endings.
intro.cn: banal 经法语携带 ban 词根；英语只给它穿上朴素的词尾。

latinIntro.en: No Latin here: the line runs Germanic bannan into Old French ban before it returns to English.
latinIntro.cn: 此处无拉丁语：词线由日耳曼 bannan 入古法语 ban，再回流英语。
